text:
Carolina had about as full a Saturday as a team can have. The Hurricanes honoured Taylor Hall for his 1,000th NHL game, fell two goals behind Edmonton, then ran the Oilers off the ice 7-4 in a matinee, a game Yahoo Sports framed as Sebastian Aho making "Remarkable Carolina Hurricanes History". Now they get on a plane for the second night of a back-to-back. They have points in six straight (5-0-1), and the process matches the results: 59% of the expected goals at five on five this season, the share of chance quality, and 67% across the last five.

The Rangers have had five days to rest and think, and they have plenty to think about. Igor Shesterkin has been out for the season since a knee injury in October, and the crease now belongs to Dylan Garand and Joonas Korpisalo, a pairing the New York Post called an "unexpected dynamic goalie tandem". Garand gets this one with a .910 save percentage and 3.5 goals saved above expected in 15 games. New York has won three straight, but the injury list keeps growing: Pavel Dorofeyev joined Oliver Bjorkstrand on injured reserve, and the club traded for center Max Sasson from Vancouver on Friday.

Carolina is down a weapon too. Nikolaj Ehlers (22 points in 23 games) is out, with Jesperi Kotkaniemi next in line for his minutes. Brandon Bussi starts in net, and his season has been rough: a .872 save percentage and 3.0 goals allowed above expected over eight games, a small sample next to a decent 39-game year last season. Sean Walker plays his 500th NHL game.

On the Rangers side, watch J.T. Miller. He has no goals in eight games on 3.4 expected goals, the kind of drought that usually ends when the chances keep coming. Our numbers have Carolina at 3.38 expected goals tonight and New York at 2.91, with the back-to-back already priced in. Our race simulations put the Rangers in the playoffs 73% of the time and have the Hurricanes all but in.
headline: Hurricanes ride a big Saturday into a rested Garden
